# Clearer audit results

## Problem statement

The audit skill's end-of-session report Conclusion section buries the readiness
verdict ("Ready for ship") at the end of a long sentence, making it easy for
operators to miss when scanning reports. The verdict needs to be visually
prominent so operators can instantly see whether the item is ready to ship or
not.

## Users

- **Operators** reviewing audit results need to see at a glance whether the
  audited item is ready to ship.
- **Producers** scanning a grid of panes need the verdict to be immediately
  visible in the Conclusion section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the session status is `completed`, the Conclusion section's first line
   is `✅ Ready to ship` (green) on its own line, followed by the completion
   sentence: `This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}).`
2. When the session status is **not** `completed`, the Conclusion section's
   first line is `🚫 Not ready to ship` (red) on its own line, followed by the
   incomplete-session sentence.
3. The green and red colouring is applied via ANSI escape sequences so that
   terminals supporting colour display the text in the correct colour, while
   plain-text terminals degrade gracefully (no garbled output).
4. All existing end-of-session reports across all skills (audit, intake, plan,
   implement, ship, …) use the new Conclusion format.
5. All existing tests for `render_report.py` pass; new tests cover the
   green/red colour formatting in both completed and incomplete states.

## Impact

Operators can now see at a glance whether an audited item is ready to ship by
looking at the colour and position of the verdict in the audit's Conclusion
section.

## Constraints

- The report renderer must work in plain-text (non-ANSI) terminals — colour
  is best-effort.
- The change must be backward-compatible with existing report consumers that
  parse the Conclusion section.
- The `next_action` parameter should no longer be appended at the end of the
  completion sentence (it is replaced by the standalone "Ready to ship" /
  "Not ready to ship" line).

## Existing state

The `render_report()` function in
`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` builds the Conclusion section as:

```
## Conclusion

This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}.
```

For incomplete sessions:

```
## Conclusion

{skill_name} session for {id} ({title}) is incomplete. Requires attention ({next_action}).
```

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Modify the `render_report()`
  function's Conclusion section to move the readiness verdict to the top,
  in green or red.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update existing tests and add
  new tests for the colour-coded Conclusion format.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via
  helper report skill (the skill that introduced the report template).
- SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)
- SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB – Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill release process (completed)
- SA-0MQ01F8OJ007HEEP – Test: AMPA audit handler writes to audit_results via wl audit-set (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What format should the "not ready" message use? — Answer: "Not ready to ship" with red colour, mirroring the "Ready to ship" green format. Source: work item description ("or its negative counterpart").
- Q: Should the `next_action` parameter still appear in the Conclusion? — Answer: No — it is replaced by the standalone verdict line. Source: work item description says to "move" the readiness line to appear first.

# audit_runner false-positive chore deduplication and needsProducerReview fix

## Problem

Every `audit_runner.py issue <id>` run that finds a medium/low severity code-quality finding classified as *candidate false positive* creates a **new** chore work item on every audit cycle. Combined with the runner's behaviour of setting `needsProducerReview = true` on every passing (`Ready to close: Yes`) top-level audit (when a prior passing audit with an identical v2 content fingerprint does not already exist), this means:

1. A backlog of 20+ duplicate chore items accumulates (same ruff rule in same file, re-created every audit run).
2. 7 of 36 in_review items on the 2026-11-02 release were blocked purely because the producer-review gate found `needsProducerReview` set by these chores — clearing the flag is manual, and the next audit re-arms it.
3. Releases cannot converge: each audit creates new chores, and each passing audit re-sets the flag.

The chore-creation path (lines ~12061–12080 in `audit_runner.py`) does **no deduplication**: it iterates `fp_screen_results` and creates a new chore for every medium/low `confident-false-positive` entry regardless of whether an identical chore already exists.

## Users

- **Release operator** — wants `/skill:ship release` to succeed without manually clearing `needsProducerReview` flags on dozens of false-positive chores.
- **Producer (Map)** — does not need to make a decision on every lint false positive every audit cycle; wants a one-time suppression mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeated audits of the same unchanged item do not create duplicate chore items — deduplicated by rule code + file path + line number + content fingerprint; proven by a test.
2. An audit ending `Ready to close: Yes` does **not** set `needsProducerReview` when the only medium/low false-positive candidate chores are already tracked (no new chores created means no flag set).
3. An accepted false positive can be recorded once (via `auditWaiver` on the parent item) and no longer triggers chore creation or flag-setting for that rule+file+line combination.
4. Release gate regression test: a repository with N accepted false-positive chores does not fail the ship producer-review gate.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Blocks `/skill:ship release` on repositories with deliberate lint patterns; each release needs manual flag clearing (2026-11-02 release: 7 items cleared by hand).

## Constraints

- Must preserve the existing `confident-false-positive` remediation path for critical/high findings (that path triggers config fixes and commits — untouched).
- Must preserve `uncertain` and `genuine` findings as blocking (no behavioural change for non-false-positives).
- `auditWaiver` field already exists on work items and can be extended for this purpose.
- Deduplication must be idempotent across audit runs — running twice in a row must yield the same chore set.

## Existing state

- `_create_chore_item()` (line 11837) creates a chore for every medium/low `confident-false-positive` finding without checking for duplicates.
- `_producer_review_required_reason()` and the lifecycle code at line ~14769 set `needsProducerReview` on every passing top-level audit unless a prior passing audit with an identical v2 content fingerprint is found.
- Medium/low CFPs are **not remediable** (they skip the config-fix loop) but are **treated as blocking** via `_has_phase1_blocking_issues` — they never block because they are excluded from the `cq_findings` severity check, but the `needsProducerReview` flag is still set on passing audits because the runner's logic does not distinguish "only medium/low CFPs present" from "genuine blocking issues".
- `auditWaiver` field exists on work items (currently `null`).

## Desired change

1. **Deduplication layer**: Before creating a chore, check whether a chore for this exact finding (rule+file+line) already exists. Use a `seen` set keyed by `rule:file:line` within the run, and prefer reusing an existing chore rather than creating a new one.
2. **Flag gating**: In the producer-review decision, when the audit passes (`Ready to close: Yes`) and the only medium/low findings are CFPs with tracking chores, do **not** set `needsProducerReview`. The flag should only be set when there is a genuine producer decision required (uncertain findings, genuine critical/high findings, or content changes).
3. **Waiver storage**: When a producer reviews and accepts a false positive, record the waiver on the parent item's `auditWaiver` field (a list of `{rule, file, line, justification, auditedAt}`). A waived finding is excluded from chore creation and from blocking checks.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing the chore-creation logic could affect downstream consumers
  that rely on one chore per finding (e.g. dashboards, reports). **Mitigation:**
  chore IDs are preserved when reusing; the audit report still records all
  findings with their classifications — only duplicate *creation* is prevented.
- **Risk:** Deduplication by rule+file+line may be too coarse if the same line
  carries multiple ruff findings for the same rule. **Mitigation:** add the
  finding message to the key if needed.
- **Assumption:** The `auditWaiver` field on work items can accept an array of
  waiver objects. Verified by inspecting the worklog schema — `auditWaiver` is
  a nullable field; extending it to a list is safe.
- **Scope:** A producer-facing UI for waivers is out of scope. The mechanism
  is data-level only (wl update --audit-waiver or programmatic).
- **Scope creep:** This item does NOT change the remediation path for
  critical/high `confident-false-positive` findings — those continue to
  trigger config fixes and commits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — main implementation changes
  - `_create_chore_item()` — add deduplication check
  - `_run_remediation_loop()` — add waiver-based filtering and deduplication
  - `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` — consider waivers
  - `_resolve_producer_review_decision()` — gate flag on "only tracked CFPs"
  - `_producer_review_preserved()` — extend to check waiver state
- `skill/audit/tests/` — new tests for deduplication, waiver, and flag-gating behaviour
- `command/` / `skill/ship/` — verify the ship gate respects waivers

## Related work

- SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR — Audit: on ruff false positive, fix the ruff config and re-run (completed)
- SA-0MST01NPD007MYG4 — Tests: false-positive screen (ruff findings) (completed)
- SA-0MST01O4G002VPBR — False-positive screen (audit Phase 1) (completed)
- SA-0MST01OX4007Z17C — Config remediation loop (ruff false positives) (completed)
- SA-0MSYPAV1R000SMHK — Bug: audit false-positive screen crashes (completed)
- SA-0MW548R9Z0012N44, SA-0MW3G6LWN009A9UY, SA-0MW529FKC009MURB, ... — Duplicate chore items currently open (examples of the problem)

# Document driven-session lock holder

## Goal

Update `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
to describe the driven-session lock-holder behaviour accurately:

1. **Who holds the lock.** During a driven child session, the long-lived
   `phase_drive` driver process holds the per-child lock (not the short-lived
   `start` subprocess inside `parent`). The lock file's recorded pid is the
   driver pid.
2. **For how long.** From immediately before the session is spawned until the
   spawner returns (success, non-zero exit or timeout).
3. **How the token reaches the session.** The driver acquires the lock with
   `_new_child_lock(child_id)`, sets it as the process's held lock via
   `_set_child_lock`, and `_child_session_env()` then propagates
   `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` to the spawned session.
4. **Failure/timeout release paths.** The lock is released in a `finally`
   block, so every spawner outcome releases it. A different live holder is
   still refused with `skipped-held` (with `held_by`/`held_children`) and no
   session is spawned.
5. **Residual window.** Document the driver-death-while-session-lives window:
   if the driver is killed while a spawned session is still working, the
   kernel releases the driver's flock and the hydrator may demote the item.
   This is an accepted residual window; option B (session-held lock) would
   close it but needs a dedicated lock-holder process.

## Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` - the per-child lock section (~line 1078-1102).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` - the per-child lock reference
  (~line 2290-2306).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (covers parent AC6): Documentation updated. `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
  and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the driven-session
  lock-holder behaviour accurately (who holds the lock, for how long, how the
  token reaches the session, and the failure/timeout release paths).
- AC2: Both files state that the driver holds the lock for the session's
  whole lifetime during a drive.
- AC3: Both files describe how the token reaches the spawned session and that
  ownership remains token-based.
- AC4: Both files describe the release paths and the driver-death residual
  window, with no contradiction against the existing lock primitive
  documentation.

## Impact

Producers and agents can read, in the implement skill and its reference, exactly who owns a driven child's lock, for how long, and which failure window remains — so a demoted child is diagnosed correctly instead of mistaken for a broken drive.

## Related

Parent: SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR

data.description:
## Problem statement

Work items that have passed through planning (stage `plan_complete`) are
sometimes left with `assignee: "Map"` (the producer identity) instead of being
cleared to empty. The plan skill's terminal transition calls
`StatusLifecycle.update_status(item_id, "open", stage="plan_complete")`
expecting the assignee to be released, but `should_release_assignee()` returns
`False` for Map because Map is classified as a producer hold. Items that
originally had Map assigned by intake (or by the herdr downtime dispatcher)
therefore retain the Map assignee after planning completes.

Evidence: MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E and MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS in tce-main-street are
both at `plan_complete` with `assignee: "Map"`.

## Users

- **herdr downtime dispatcher** — auto-dispatches items for processing; items
  stranded with Map cannot be re-dispatched because a non-empty assignee is a
  scheduling hold.
- **Map (producer)** — the producer has decided that `Map` is **not** a
  persistent hold marker: a lingering `Map` assignee after a skill run is
  indistinguishable from a deliberate producer park and strands the item.
- **Agents running any skill** — need one consistent rule: every terminal
  transition releases the assignee, so no skill can leave a scheduling hold
  behind on success or failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every skill terminal transition — **success or failure** — clears the
   persisted `assignee` to empty, including when the assignee is `Map`.
2. The rule applies to **all skills** (intake, plan, implement, audit,
   find-related, effort-and-risk, refactor, and any future skill), not only the
   plan skill.
3. The release is enforced in the shared terminal-transition choke point
   (`StatusLifecycle.update_status` and the context-manager exit paths) so a
   skill cannot reintroduce the hold by omission or by using a direct durable
   write.
4. `needsProducerReview` remains the **only** persistent-hold signal: releasing
   the assignee must never clear the `needsProducerReview` flag, and a
   `needsProducerReview` item must still be observable as awaiting producer
   review after its assignee is released.
5. Regression tests cover, table-driven across skills, both success and
   failure terminal paths and assert that a pre-existing `Map` assignee is
   released while the `needsProducerReview` flag survives.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (assignee-release invariant), `README`, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular any text that currently
   describes `Map` as a persistent producer hold.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Items that finish any skill run — successful or failed — are always released
for dispatch, so planned and implemented work no longer gets stranded behind a
lingering `Map` assignee.

## Constraints

- `Map` is no longer a persistent-hold marker; the producer's deliberate hold
  is represented by `needsProducerReview` alone (producer decision, this
  intake).
- The change must be in shared infrastructure (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
  and `skill/shared/claim_release.py`), not per-skill patches.
- The existing backstops (session-end `release_session_claim`, `signal_release`,
  `reap_stale_claims`) must stay consistent with the same predicate.
- Scope-creep risk: broader claim-lifecycle rework (e.g. dispatcher identity
  handling) is out of scope and should be recorded as linked work items.

## Existing state

- `StatusLifecycle.update_status()` with `release_assignee=None` calls
  `should_release_assignee()`, which returns `False` for Map, so Map is never
  cleared by the automatic release mechanism.
- The plan skill SKILL.md documents: "the terminal transitions below release any
  claim the item already carried", but the implementation does not release Map.
- The plan skill claims with no assignee itself — the Map is inherited from
  intake or from the herdr downtime dispatcher.
- `should_release_assignee()` is shared by all release paths (lifecycle, session
  backstop, reaper), so it is the single predicate to change.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` currently describe `Map`
  as a sanctioned persistent hold — that documentation is now wrong and must be
  updated.

## Desired change

Remove the producer-assignee exemption from the release predicate so that every
terminal transition (success or failure) releases any assignee, including
`Map`, in the shared choke point. Keep `needsProducerReview` as the sole
persistent-hold signal, and update the invariant documentation and regression
matrix accordingly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `should_release_assignee()`,
  `is_producer_assignee()`, `_release_skip_reason()`, `release_claim()`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status()`,
  `_auto_release_requested()`, `_should_release_assignee()`, `_restore_original()`
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — assignee-release invariant wording (Map no longer a hold)
- `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` — invariant reference documentation
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — plan status-lifecycle section
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — implement status-lifecycle section
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — intake assignee-release note
- `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — regression matrix (success +
  failure, Map pre-claim)

## Related work

- SA-0MW0F91KN004J06U: Remove assignee when a session finishes (completed)
- SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH: Enforce assignee release on every terminal outcome across all skills (completed)
- SA-0MW0X5W01008IY7Z: Close coverage gap: Release covers any non-producer claim (completed)
- SA-0MVVF7CZ6002UDKU: Document the assignee-release invariant (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6GWG005VIFK: T1: Table-driven assignee-release regression matrix (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL: Flip StatusLifecycle assignee-release default (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ: Migrate callers and pin intentional holds (completed)
- SA-0MVVF75ZA007XNKB: Release assignee on signal, timeout and drive paths (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the assignee-release invariant apply to `Map` when a work item
  transitions to `plan_complete` (i.e. should `Map` be released at planning
  completion), or should `Map` always be preserved as a persistent producer
  hold regardless of stage?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): "yes release the assignee, *always*
  whether a skill succeeds or fails."
- Q: "If `Map` should be released at `plan_complete`, should the fix adjust
  `should_release_assignee()` (shared predicate) or have the plan skill
  explicitly clear the assignee in its terminal transition?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): "in terminal transitions, whether
  success or failure."
- Q: "Does this apply only to the plan skill, or to all skills (implement,
  intake, audit) that inherit a `Map` assignee?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): "all skills."

Research: inspected `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` and
`skill/shared/claim_release.py`; confirmed `should_release_assignee()` returns
`False` for `Map` (`is_producer_assignee`) and that all release paths share
that predicate. Inspected the two cited items in
`../tce-main-street` (`MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`, `MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS`) and
confirmed both sit at `plan_complete` with `assignee: "Map"`.

Documented assumption: since `Map` is no longer a hold marker, the
`needsProducerReview` flag is the sole persistent-hold signal. Releasing the
assignee on a `needsProducerReview` handoff therefore does not lose the
producer's intent — the flag still holds the item for producer review. The
`needsProducerReview` flag must never be cleared by the release.
